title: Irrigation and Water Management in Lowland and Upland Rice
source: ICAR - Indian Institute of Water Management (IIWM), Bhubaneswar
content: Total water requirement for transplanted puddled rice ranges from 1200 mm to 1500 mm depending on soil texture and climate. Continuous submergence of 5 cm water is unnecessary and wastes water. Adopt Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) using a field water tube (pani pipe). Critical growth stages sensitive to moisture stress: 1. Panicle initiation stage (40-50 DAT), 2. Booting stage, 3. Flowering and heading stage, and 4. Milk/grain filling stage. Drought stress at flowering induces high spikelet sterility. Water management guideline: Keep 2-3 cm shallow water during initial 10 days after transplanting for root establishment. During tillering, introduce intermittent irrigation (irrigate 2-3 days after ponded water has disappeared). Maintain 3-5 cm standing water strictly during panicle initiation to flowering. Drain water completely 10-15 days before harvest to facilitate uniform ripening and mechanical harvesting. Caution: In saline soils, continuous shallow ponding is necessary to suppress salinity.
